content:
Let \(s=p+q\). Then \(r=s+1\). Substituting into \(pq+qr+rp=191\):
\[
pq+q(s+1)+p(s+1)=191
\]
so
\[
s^2+pq+s=191.
\]
Thus
\[
pq=191-s^2-s.
\]
Since \(pq>0\), \(s^2+s<191\), so \(s\le 13\). Also \(p,q\) are odd primes (if one were 2, \(r\) would be even and composite), so \(s\) is even. Check \(s=6,8,10,12\):

- \(s=6\): \(pq=149\), discriminant negative.
- \(s=8\): \(pq=119\), discriminant negative.
- \(s=10\): \(pq=81\), discriminant negative.
- \(s=12\): \(pq=35\), so \(\{p,q\}=\{5,7\}\), and \(r=13\).

Check: \(5\cdot7+7\cdot13+13\cdot5=35+91+65=191\). Thus:
\[
p+q+r=5+7+13=25.
\]

\[
\boxed{25}
\]
